source: https://cwe.mitre.org/ (curated subset relevant to Java applications and their dependencies)

CWE-20.name: Improper Input Validation
CWE-20.description: The product receives input but does not validate, or incorrectly validates, that it has the properties required to process it safely.
CWE-20.fix: Validate all external input against an allow-list of expected type, length, format and range before using it.

CWE-22.name: Path Traversal
CWE-22.description: A pathname is built from external input without neutralizing sequences such as '../', so it can resolve to a location outside the restricted directory.
CWE-22.fix: Resolve the path against a fixed base directory, canonicalize it and reject it unless it still starts with the base directory. Prefer mapping user input to an allow-list of file names.

CWE-77.name: Command Injection
CWE-77.description: A command is constructed from externally influenced input without neutralizing special elements that change the command.
CWE-77.fix: Avoid building command strings; call a library API instead, or pass fixed arguments as an array after allow-list validation.

CWE-78.name: OS Command Injection
CWE-78.description: An operating system command is built from external input, letting an attacker run arbitrary commands with the application's privileges.
CWE-78.fix: Do not pass user input to Runtime.exec or a shell. Use a Java API for the task, or validate the input against a strict allow-list and pass it as a separate argument to ProcessBuilder without invoking a shell.

CWE-79.name: Cross-site Scripting (XSS)
CWE-79.description: User-controllable input is placed in a web page without neutralization, so it executes as script in other users' browsers.
CWE-79.fix: Encode output for the context (HTML body, attribute, JavaScript, URL) with a vetted encoder such as the OWASP Java Encoder, and use templating engines with auto-escaping.

CWE-89.name: SQL Injection
CWE-89.description: An SQL command is built from external input without neutralization, so the input can change the query's logic, read or modify data, or run administrative operations.
CWE-89.fix: Use parameterized queries (PreparedStatement with ? placeholders, JPA named parameters, or Spring JdbcTemplate arguments). Never concatenate input into SQL. Apply least-privilege database accounts.

CWE-94.name: Code Injection
CWE-94.description: Code is generated or evaluated from external input, allowing an attacker to run arbitrary code.
CWE-94.fix: Never evaluate user input as code or expressions; restrict expression languages to a safe, sandboxed subset.

CWE-113.name: HTTP Response Splitting
CWE-113.description: CR/LF characters from external input are written into HTTP headers.
CWE-113.fix: Strip or reject CR and LF characters before writing input into headers; use framework APIs that validate header values.

CWE-117.name: Log Injection
CWE-117.description: Unsanitized input is written to logs, allowing forged log entries.
CWE-117.fix: Encode or strip newline characters from input before logging, or use structured logging.

CWE-200.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information
CWE-200.description: Sensitive information is exposed to an actor that is not authorized to access it.
CWE-200.fix: Return generic messages to clients and keep sensitive details in protected server-side logs.

CWE-209.name: Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
CWE-209.description: Error messages or stack traces reveal implementation details that help an attacker.
CWE-209.fix: Log exceptions with a logging framework and show users a generic error message; never print stack traces to responses or standard output in production.

CWE-259.name: Hard-coded Password
CWE-259.description: A password is embedded in the source code.
CWE-259.fix: Load passwords from environment variables or a secret manager and rotate the exposed one.

CWE-287.name: Improper Authentication
CWE-287.description: The product does not prove, or insufficiently proves, that an actor's claimed identity is correct.
CWE-287.fix: Use a vetted authentication framework (e.g. Spring Security) and verify credentials and tokens on every request.

CWE-295.name: Improper Certificate Validation
CWE-295.description: TLS certificates are not validated, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.
CWE-295.fix: Do not install trust-all TrustManagers or HostnameVerifiers; use the platform defaults.

CWE-321.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
CWE-321.description: A cryptographic key is embedded in the code, so anyone with access to the code or binary can decrypt data or forge signatures (for example JWTs).
CWE-321.fix: Generate keys with a secure random source and load them from a key store, KMS or environment secret at runtime. Rotate the exposed key.
CWE-321.example:
byte[] key = Base64.getDecoder().decode(System.getenv("JWT_SIGNING_KEY"));
SecretKeySpec spec = new SecretKeySpec(key, "HmacSHA256");

CWE-327.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-327.description: The code uses a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm or mode (DES, RC4, ECB, old TLS versions), which can expose sensitive data.
CWE-327.fix: Use modern authenticated encryption such as AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random 12-byte IV and 256-bit keys, and TLS 1.2+.

CWE-328.name: Use of Weak Hash
CWE-328.description: A weak hash algorithm (MD5, SHA-1) is used where collision or preimage resistance is needed, such as for passwords or integrity checks.
CWE-328.fix: Use SHA-256 or better for integrity, and a slow salted password hash (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 or PBKDF2) for passwords.
CWE-328.example:
PasswordEncoder encoder = new BCryptPasswordEncoder();
String hash = encoder.encode(rawPassword);

CWE-329.name: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode
CWE-329.description: The initialization vector is constant or predictable, weakening the encryption.
CWE-329.fix: Generate a fresh random IV with SecureRandom for every encryption and store it alongside the ciphertext.

CWE-330.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
CWE-330.description: Predictable random values are used in a security context.
CWE-330.fix: Use java.security.SecureRandom for tokens, keys and identifiers.

CWE-352.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
CWE-352.description: The application does not verify that a state-changing request was intentionally made by the user.
CWE-352.fix: Enable CSRF protection (synchronizer tokens or SameSite cookies) for state-changing requests.

CWE-400.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
CWE-400.description: Input can make the component consume excessive CPU, memory or other resources (denial of service).
CWE-400.fix: Upgrade the affected component and enforce input size and rate limits.

CWE-434.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CWE-434.description: Uploaded files are not restricted by type, allowing executable content.
CWE-434.fix: Validate file type by content, store uploads outside the web root with generated names.

CWE-502.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CWE-502.description: Untrusted data is deserialized with a mechanism that can instantiate arbitrary classes, enabling gadget-chain attacks up to remote code execution.
CWE-502.fix: Do not deserialize untrusted data with ObjectInputStream, XMLDecoder or unrestricted polymorphic JSON. Use data-only formats (JSON into fixed DTOs) or apply an allow-list ObjectInputFilter.

CWE-532.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
CWE-532.description: Sensitive data such as passwords or tokens is written to logs.
CWE-532.fix: Mask or omit secrets and personal data before logging.

CWE-547.name: Use of Hard-coded, Security-relevant Constants
CWE-547.description: Security-relevant values such as IP addresses are hard-coded, making the code brittle and exposing infrastructure details.
CWE-547.fix: Move addresses and other environment-specific values into configuration.

CWE-601.name: Open Redirect
CWE-601.description: The application redirects to a URL taken from user input.
CWE-601.fix: Redirect only to relative paths or to an allow-list of trusted destinations.

CWE-611.name: XML External Entity (XXE)
CWE-611.description: An XML parser processes external entities from untrusted documents, allowing file disclosure or SSRF.
CWE-611.fix: Disable DOCTYPE declarations and external entities on the parser factory (disallow-doctype-decl = true).

CWE-643.name: XPath Injection
CWE-643.description: XPath expressions are built from external input.
CWE-643.fix: Use parameterized XPath (XPathVariableResolver) and validate input.

CWE-674.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
CWE-674.description: Crafted input causes deep recursion and a stack overflow (denial of service).
CWE-674.fix: Upgrade the affected component and limit nesting depth of parsed input.

CWE-770.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits
CWE-770.description: Resources are allocated without limits, enabling denial of service.
CWE-770.fix: Upgrade the affected component and enforce quotas and size limits.

CWE-798.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-798.description: Credentials such as passwords, API keys or tokens are embedded in the source code, where anyone with repository or binary access can read and reuse them.
CWE-798.fix: Remove the secret from the code and git history, rotate it, and read it at runtime from environment variables, a secrets manager or the platform's credential store.

CWE-862.name: Missing Authorization
CWE-862.description: The product does not check whether the actor is allowed to perform an action.
CWE-862.fix: Enforce authorization checks on every protected endpoint and resource.

CWE-917.name: Expression Language Injection
CWE-917.description: Input is evaluated by an expression language (for example JNDI lookups in Log4j message patterns), enabling remote code execution.
CWE-917.fix: Upgrade the affected library and never evaluate expressions built from user input.

CWE-918.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
CWE-918.description: The server fetches a URL supplied by the user, letting attackers reach internal services.
CWE-918.fix: Validate destination hosts against an allow-list and block internal address ranges.

CWE-1104.name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
CWE-1104.description: The product relies on components that are outdated or no longer maintained.
CWE-1104.fix: Upgrade to a supported release and track dependencies with automated update tooling.

CWE-1333.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity (ReDoS)
CWE-1333.description: A regular expression with catastrophic backtracking can be exploited for denial of service.
CWE-1333.fix: Upgrade the affected component or rewrite the expression to avoid nested quantifiers.
